This role sits within the Product organization and will work closely with teams across Plan, Source Code Management, Code Review, and AI. We are focused on helping GitLab customers plan, build, and deliver software in a faster, more connected way.

You'll join a group that is rethinking how planning and coding should work as AI changes the speed and shape of software development. Rather than treating planning, coding, and review as separate stages, we're exploring how to bring these workflows closer together so humans and agents can collaborate more effectively.

An overview of this role

As a Senior Product Manager, you will own GitLab's Secret Detection offering and the Vulnerability Research function that produces the detection content across security products. Secret Detection is one of the highest-signal, highest-volume security capabilities on the platform. Leaked credentials are the most common initial access vector in real breaches, and as AI agents write, commit, and configure more of the software, the surface area for exposed secrets grows faster than the number of humans watching it.

You will own the full loop: detect a secret with high precision, tell the customer whether it is still live, get it revoked, and prevent the next one from ever landing. In parallel, you will own vulnerability research as a product asset rather than a back-office function. The detection rules, advisory data, and malicious package and reference intelligence your team produces are what make GitLab's security scanners worth paying for, and they need to ship on a cadence with measurable quality.

This is an outcome-owning role - you will carry adoption, retention, and revenue targets for your area and be expected to explain how your roadmap moves them.

Some examples of our projects:

  • Push protection and pre-receive blocking that stops a credential before it reaches a repository, without wrecking developer flow
  • Secret validity checking and automated revocation partnerships with major cloud and SaaS token issuers
  • Detection content pipelines that turn threat research into shipped rules, with precision and recall tracked per rule
  • Intelligence-driven detection of malicious packages, dependencies, and references entering the software supply chain

What you'll do

  • Own the business outcomes for Secret Detection and Vulnerability Research, including adoption, expansion, competitive win rate, and revenue contribution. Bring a point of view on packaging and pricing, not just features.
  • Set the strategy for the full secret lifecycle: prevention, detection, validation, revocation, and reporting across GitLab.com, Dedicated, and Self-Managed.
  • Treat detection content as a product. Define how rules, advisories, and intelligence feeds are sourced, validated, versioned, and measured, and make quality visible to customers.
  • Hold the line on detection quality. False positives are a product defect and you will own the metrics that prove precision is improving.
  • Work at the level of the technology. Read the rule syntax, question the entropy heuristics, understand why a scanner missed something, and challenge engineering with informed alternatives.
  • Use AI to compress the distance between question and answer. Pull your own data, prototype your own flows, synthesize research and competitive input yourself, and bring conclusions rather than requests for someone else to investigate.
  • Build the case for where AI belongs in the product: triage, rule generation, remediation guidance, and reducing the human review burden per finding.
  • Partner with engineering, security research, threat intelligence, Field, and GitLab's own Security team, who are one of your most demanding users.
  • Communicate in writing, asynchronously, with enough precision that a distributed team can act without a meeting.

What you'll bring

  • Domain depth in application security, vulnerability management, or security research. You have worked on or adjacent to scanners, detection content, threat intelligence, or SDLC security tooling and you know how these products actually get evaluated in a bake-off.
  • Technical credibility sufficient to earn the respect of a security engineering team. You do not need to have written the scanner, but you should be able to reason about detection logic, data pipelines, CI integration, and the tradeoffs between coverage and noise.
  • Commercial reasoning. You start from revenue mechanics, buyer motion, and competitive displacement, then work inward to product decisions. Candidates who reason only from feature lists outward are not a fit.
  • Evidence of using AI as a force multiplier in your own work: research, analysis, data pulls, prototyping, drafting. Consuming a chat assistant occasionally is not the same as restructuring how you work.
  • Judgment under ambiguity. You bring structured options and a recommendation instead of escalating an open question.
  • Bias for clarity. You can take a noisy, technical, politically contested problem and produce one page that everyone can align on.
  • Bonus: hands-on background as a developer, security engineer, red teamer, or researcher; experience with credential and token ecosystems; experience commercializing a data or intelligence asset.

About the team

This role sits in GitLab's Security product management organization, which owns application security testing, vulnerability management, supply chain security, secrets management, and AI governance. The Security Section is central to GitLab's Ultimate tier and to the shift toward consumption-based product revenue, so the work is visible to senior leadership and directly tied to company results. You will work asynchronously with engineering, design, and research counterparts across multiple regions, and with the Field teams who take this to market.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

From day one, we've been breaking down barriers, empowering people with the tools, knowledge, and products to participate in the financial system. Our innovation doesn't stop — and we need bright, curious minds to help shape the future of finance!

As an Associate Product Manager, you'll be at the center of our product innovation. You'll work alongside top talent from engineering, design, research, and more to bring groundbreaking financial products to life. From simplifying complex financial processes to crafting seamless customer experiences, your work will help shape the future of fintech. This role offers direct mentorship from some of the most accomplished product leaders in the industry, giving you the chance to grow, learn, and make a real impact in a fast-paced, cutting-edge environment.

This role is based in our New York, NY office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

  • Collaborate with engineering, design, research, data science, and marketing teams to deeply understand our customers and their most pressing needs
  • Define and execute product strategies that align with business goals and user expectations
  • Be the voice of the product, facilitating communication and collaboration across teams
  • Lead product launches, ensuring they are delivered on time and meet a high standard of quality
  • Set and monitor KPIs to measure success and track product engagement and adoption

What you bring

  • Currently enrolled in a full-time, degree-seeking program in Engineering, Computer Science, Business, Economics, or a related field, graduating between Winter 2026 and Summer 2027
  • 0–1 years of experience in product management, product development, or related roles; internship or co-op experience in fintech or tech is a plus
  • Sharp analytical and technical skills, a problem-solving mindset, and the ability to make data-driven decisions
  • Demonstrated leadership and communication abilities, with experience thriving in collaborative, cross-functional teams
  • An entrepreneurial spirit — takes ownership of projects, turns ideas into action, and drives innovation
  • A passion for fintech and a desire to learn more about financial products, markets, and emerging technologies

What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career
  • Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching
  • Top tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents
  • Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds
  • Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not
  • Lifestyle wallet — a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more
  • Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits
  • Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more!

title: Technical Program Manager, Hardware Systems
description:
About Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. Working across the full model and systems stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the physical constraints of real-world systems to improve people’s lives.

About the Role

We are looking for a Member of Technical Program Staff to drive the development, prototyping, and integration of innovative hardware solutions used for data collection as well as robotic systems. You will work closely with mechanical, electrical, test, manufacturing, and supply chain teams to set functional requirements, coordinate hardware iterations, and move solutions from prototype through early production.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA and requires in-person presence 4 days a week.

In this role you will:

  • Drive functional requirements for various end effector sub-systems, sensing technologies, integration of various peripherals into one system to drive data collection for model development, related milestones, and validation criteria.

  • Collaborate with research teams, align system-level integration requirements, deliverables, calibration needs, configurations to test, etc.

  • Work closely with the operations team in getting the data collection hardware rolled out, monitor the field failures as those pop-up and make sure the right stakeholders are involved in resolution.

  • Coordinate the design and integration of tactile sensing materials, mechanical structures, PCBAs, interconnects, harnesses, and signal paths into robotic systems.

  • Establish effective mechanisms for design reviews, drawing and documentation readiness, change control, design releases, decision tracking, characterization and validation readiness, and production readiness.

  • Partner with manufacturing, test, and supply chain on prototype builds, assembly constraints, DFM/DFA, end-of-line test requirements, equipment lead times, handoffs, and the transition to manufacturable assemblies.

  • Drive tradeoff decisions with the right stakeholders across material selection, mechanical performance, functionality, reliability, scaling, cost, quality, schedule, and lead time for both robot and data collection hardware by collaborating cross-functionally and quantifying impact to the program.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Understand material properties, compliance, bonding, packaging, tolerances, and integration constraints that affect tactile sensor performance in robotic systems.

  • Have experience integrating PCBAs, interconnects, small form factor connectors, analog signals, and EMI-sensitive hardware into compact mechanical assemblies.

  • Enjoy occasional hands-on work as well planning for building, testing, and debugging physical systems, including characterization and validation setups, calibration, durability, signal quality, and failure modes.

  • Have led complex electromechanical hardware programs from evolving requirements through prototype builds and manufacturing.

  • Understand the deliverables for data collection hardware, manage expectations and fast iterations, have had to make judgment calls without having to wait for a decision to emerge from large meetings to keep things moving.

What success looks like:

  • Functional requirements, mechanical interfaces, performance targets, characterization plans, validation plans, and reliability goals are aligned across engineering teams.

  • Fit, alignment, bonding, wear, signal integrity, EMI, calibration, durability, functionality, reliability, and scaling risks are surfaced early and driven to closure.

  • Design reviews, drawings, documentation, change control, characterization and validation setups, and production-release mechanisms are operating effectively.

  • Prototype builds transition toward manufacturable assemblies with DFM/DFA, end-of-line test requirements, equipment lead times, and cross-functional tradeoffs quantified and resolved.

  • Supply chain risks are well accounted for, manufacturing process or design improvements are well rationalized with as clear scope as possible for a given phase, hardware and firmware teams are aligned on priorities across multiple systems.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

title: Program Manager, Government Trusted Access
description:
About the Team

OpenAI for Government works with U.S. and allied government institutions to support the responsible adoption of AI across defense, intelligence, federal civilian, state and local, and international public-sector missions. We help public servants use frontier AI in ways that are effective, trusted, and grounded in real-world requirements for safety, reliability, security, compliance, and accountability.

Government Trusted Access programs help eligible public-sector organizations and practitioners use advanced capabilities for approved, high-value work in sensitive domains. These programs bring together OpenAI for Government, Product Policy, Legal, Security, International, Research, User Operations, Technical Success, Global Affairs, and domain experts. Each program has distinct eligibility criteria, safeguards, and decision owners; our job is to make the overall government experience coherent and executable.

About the Role

We are seeking a Program Manager to coordinate OpenAI’s Government Trusted Access portfolio across high-trust domains, such as cyber and bio. You will build and run the operating mechanisms that move government participants from initial interest through review, onboarding, activation, ongoing support, and program improvement.

The right person is a highly organized, low-ego operator who can move between strategy and detail. You are comfortable working across technical, policy, legal, safety, security, customer, and operational teams; you build durable systems without adding unnecessary process; and you communicate clearly when facts, ownership, or requirements are still evolving.

This role is based in Washington, DC. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Coordinate government participation across domain-specific Trusted Access programs, including cyber and biology, while helping stand up future programs as the portfolio evolves.

  • Own the end-to-end program operating rhythm across intake, qualification, review, approval, onboarding, activation, ongoing support, renewal, and offboarding.

  • Maintain a clear portfolio view of applicants and participating organizations, access levels, requirements, owners, dependencies, commitments, risks, and decisions needed.

  • Build practical program mechanisms such as roadmaps, ownership maps, decision logs, risk registers, service standards, operating reviews, dashboards, and executive updates.

  • Coordinate cross-functional reviews across OpenAI for Government, Safety, Product Policy, Legal, Security, Product, Research, User Operations, Technical Success, Global Affairs, and domain experts.

  • Preserve clear decision boundaries: ensure the right domain owner makes eligibility, policy, safety, security, and access decisions while keeping the broader process moving.

  • Identify stalled reviews, broken handoffs, unclear ownership, capacity constraints, and recurring operational gaps; bring the right context, options, and recommendation to resolve them.

  • Partner with government-facing teams to set accurate expectations, coordinate participant communications, and ensure commitments are tracked through completion.

  • Define and monitor program health through measures such as review time, backlog age, onboarding completion, activation, support demand, participant outcomes, and operational risk.

  • Turn manual and one-off work into scalable workflows, documentation, training, automation, and tooling while retaining appropriate human judgment for sensitive decisions.

  • Capture lessons across domains and translate them into reusable operating patterns without flattening meaningful differences between programs.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Hold an active TS clearance

  • Have 5–10 years of experience in program management, strategy and operations, product operations, trust and safety, risk operations, support operations, government technology, implementation, or a related field.

  • Have led complex, cross-functional programs from an ambiguous problem statement through launch and steady-state operation.

  • Can build trust and drive alignment without direct authority while keeping ownership, accountability, and escalation paths clear.

  • Can translate technical, policy, legal, safety, security, and customer requirements into practical workflows and decision structures.

  • Are analytically fluent and comfortable using operational data, dashboards, case-management systems, and lightweight automation to identify bottlenecks and improve program health.

  • Communicate clearly and directly with technical teams, operators, government stakeholders, and executives, especially when evidence is incomplete or tradeoffs are sensitive.

  • Learn unfamiliar domains quickly, ask strong questions, and know when to bring in specialists rather than overstate your own expertise.

  • Operate calmly in a fast-moving environment, exercise sound judgment with sensitive information, and follow through reliably on details and commitments.

title: Senior Compliance Program Manager, Political Law
region: San Francisco, CA / New York City, NY / Washington, DC
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's Integrity & Compliance function is building the systems that let us scale responsibly as our products reach more people, more enterprises, and more governments. Corporate Compliance is a key pillar of that function, covering anti-bribery and anti-corruption, conflicts of interest, gifts and hospitality, outside activities, the Code of Conduct, and related employee-conduct matters.

As Senior Compliance Program Manager, you will build and run Anthropic's political law compliance program — the operating infrastructure behind our corporate PAC, corporate political giving, state and local pay-to-play preclearance, and the gift and ethics rules governing our interactions with public officials. As the program develops, the role may also extend to oversight of lobbying registration and reporting. You'll own the program end to end: designing the workflows, registers and controls, doing the work directly where it belongs in-house, and directing and quality-checking outside political law counsel and compliance vendors where we use them. You'll be the day-to-day compliance partner to our Policy and Government Affairs teams, working in close partnership with Policy Legal, who own the substantive legal advice, and with the rest of Corporate Compliance on the anti-corruption side of government engagement.

Because we run lean, you may support certain workstreams in our broader corporate compliance program — gifts and hospitality, conflicts of interest, outside business activities and related day-to-day matters — and help design the AI-assisted workflows that let a small team cover a large surface area.

This is a builder's role. We're looking for someone who has run political law compliance programs hands-on, is equally comfortable doing the work and managing outside firms who do it, always knows where every preclearance request and filing stands, and can turn fifty-state complexity into simple processes the business will actually use.

Key responsibilities

  • Own the political contributions preclearance program: intake, covered-persons register, jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction pay-to-play screening against live and prospective public-sector business, recordkeeping, and periodic reconciliation

  • Support corporate PAC compliance operations in partnership with Policy, Finance and outside counsel — restricted-class eligibility controls, solicitation review workflow, FEC reporting oversight, and reconciliations

  • Maintain the corporate political giving log and vetting workflow for candidate, committee, 527 and c4 contributions, and integrate pay-to-play triggers into contract intake for public-sector deals

  • Depending on how the program is scoped, support or take on lobbying compliance oversight: keeping a consolidated view of registrations, deadlines and filing status, and working with the outside firms that prepare filings

  • Manage outside political law counsel and compliance vendors supporting these workstreams — scoping, inputs, quality, timeliness and budget — and recommend over time what should sit in-house versus outside

  • Run gifts and hospitality review for events and interactions involving public officials, applying federal, state and local gift and ethics rules alongside our anti-corruption standards; disposition routine matters and escalate edge cases

  • Review and disposition conflicts of interest, outside business activity and gifts and hospitality matters across the broader corporate compliance queue; help maintain the post-government-employment and recusal tracker

  • Build and deliver training, quick-reference guidance and intake how-tos for Policy, GTM and leadership; keep policies and procedures current as the footprint changes

  • Serve as product owner for AI-assisted intake, screening and case-management workflows in your areas — define requirements, run testing, decide what is automated versus human-reviewed, and report program metrics to leadership

  • Spot legal questions early and route them to Policy Legal or outside counsel with the facts assembled; keep I&C, Legal and outside counsel calibrated on risk

Minimum qualifications

  • Hands-on ownership of political law compliance programs — corporate PAC, campaign finance, pay-to-play preclearance and covered-persons tracking, lobbying registration and reporting, government gift and ethics rules — or a closely comparable multi-jurisdiction regulatory program

  • Track record building a program, not just operating one — designing preclearance or disclosure workflows, registers, filing calendars and controls from scratch or through a major redesign

  • Fluent enough to do the work directly and experienced enough to manage outside counsel and compliance vendors doing it — scoping, feeding inputs, checking quality, holding deadlines

  • Working fluency in the federal framework (FECA/FEC, LDA/HLOGA, House and Senate gift rules) and the shape of state and local variation; knows when a question is a legal call and hands it off cleanly

  • Strong project management and cross-functional execution with Policy/Government Affairs, Legal, Finance and executive stakeholders; clear, brief, business-usable writing

  • Sound judgment and discretion handling politically and personally sensitive information

Preferred qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in compliance program management

  • Experience in a corporate government affairs compliance function, a political law practice or compliance vendor, or a financial-services pay-to-play program (SEC Rule 206(4)-5, MSRB G-37, CFTC)

  • Range across the broader corporate compliance portfolio — gifts and hospitality, conflicts of interest, outside activities, anti-corruption — and appetite to learn what you haven't done yet

  • Exposure to non-US lobbying transparency regimes (EU Transparency Register, German Lobby register, Irish Regulation of Lobbying Act, UK)

  • Hands-on with compliance tooling (case management, GRC, disclosure platforms, workflow automation) and real interest in using AI to run compliance work better

  • Experience at a high-growth or technology company, or otherwise operating lean without large-team infrastructure

  • Relevant certification (e.g., CCEP) or paralegal/JD background is a plus, not a requirement; this is a program role, not a counsel role

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$255,000—$270,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

title: Supply Chain Operations Program Manager, AI Infrastructure
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.
About the Role

We are seeking a Operations Program Manager (OPM) to serve as the single-threaded operational leader for new hardware introductions (NPI) and production ramps across OpenAI’s AI infrastructure systems.

This role combines hands-on execution with strategic ownership. You will be responsible for defining the operating model, aligning cross-functional stakeholders, setting the critical path, making informed tradeoffs, escalating decisively, and ensuring hardware programs deliver on schedule, quality, cost, and scalability.

Success in this role requires comfort operating in ambiguity, influencing without authority, and driving alignment across internal teams and external partners—while keeping eyes firmly on long-term system scalability and repeatability.
In this role, you will:

Strategic & Leadership Ownership

  • Act as the single-threaded owner for operational readiness across NPI and ramp, accountable for outcomes from early bring-up through sustained production

  • Translate OpenAI’s infrastructure strategy and engineering objectives into clear operating plans, execution priorities, and decision frameworks

  • Drive alignment across Engineering, Operations, Strategic Sourcing, Finance, Capacity Planning, and Executive stakeholders by framing tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations

  • Proactively identify inflection points where decisions or investments are required to protect long-term scale, reliability, or cost targets

  • Influence operational strategy with manufacturing partners by setting expectations on execution rigor, accountability, and continuous improvement

Program Execution & Operational Excellence

  • Drive overall NPI build readiness, including material accountability, manufacturing and test readiness, product data availability, factory infrastructure, and qualification plans

  • Lead transition activities from NPI to mass production, partnering closely with Sustaining Operations teams to ensure seamless ownership transfer

title: Program Manager, Safeguards Workforce Operations
region: San Francisco, CA / Seattle, WA / New York City, NY / Washington, DC
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic’s Safeguards Enforcement team detects and mitigates misuse of Claude, and much of that work depends on people: a growing human review workforce made up of full-time staff, contractors, vendors and BPO partners. As that workforce scales across a widening range of harm areas, the programs that bring people in, give them the right access, and roll them off cleanly have to keep pace.

As Program Manager for Safeguards Workforce Operations, you’ll own those programs end to end. You’ll run onboarding, offboarding, device provisioning and access provisioning for every worker type we use, working hands-on with the requests themselves while you build the processes that make them repeatable. You’ll partner with Enforcement leads to turn shifting priorities into capacity plans, and carry those plans through with our vendor partners. Because this role supports every Safeguards Enforcement program, you’ll also connect the dots across Anthropic, working with IT, People Operations, Security, Contingent Workforce, Human Data Operations and other teams running scaled human review to streamline practices and keep standards consistent.

This is a role for someone who likes fixing broken things at speed. The landscape moves quickly, priorities change often, and the work is an even mix of direct execution and program building.

Key responsibilities

  • Own the workforce lifecycle for contractor, vendor and BPO reviewers: onboarding, offboarding, device provisioning and access provisioning

  • Triage and execute inbound requests for new or changing vendor, BPO and contractor capacity

  • Turn ad hoc or broken processes into scalable ones, with clear owners, service levels and a system of record

  • Partner with IT and Security on access governance: least-privilege provisioning, timely revocation and regular access reviews

  • Build and maintain capacity plans with Enforcement leads, translating review demand into workforce needs and adjusting as priorities shift

  • Work with Safeguards vendor management to hold partners accountable to capacity and onboarding commitments

  • Align practices with Human Data Operations and other teams running scaled human review, and help them streamline their own workflows

  • Help define the long-term workforce strategy for Safeguards Enforcement

Minimum qualifications

  • Have personally run onboarding, offboarding, access and device provisioning for contractor, vendor or BPO workforces — doing the work, not only overseeing it

  • Have operated scaled human review programs with vendors or BPOs, such as trust & safety, content moderation or data annotation operations

  • Have taken a broken or ad hoc process, made it scalable, and brought other teams along in adopting it

  • Understand the fundamentals of capacity planning: how volume, handle time, quality targets, ramp and attrition turn into workforce needs

  • Exercise sound judgment on access and permissions, and know when to bring in IT or Security

  • Move quickly and stay effective when priorities change and information is incomplete

  • Build alignment through direct partnership with the teams you depend on

Preferred qualifications

  • Owned a vendor or BPO relationship directly, including service levels and business reviews

  • Built formal capacity models for review or operations workforces

  • Supported workforces across more than one enforcement or harm area

  • Hands-on experience with device management and identity and access tooling

  • Worked through a period of hypergrowth where programs had to mature alongside the organization

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$245,000—$285,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

title: Rosalind Life Sciences Product Manager

Life sciences is one of the clearest areas where advances in intelligence can meaningfully benefit the world at large. The OpenAI Life Sciences team works at the intersection of advancing frontier life sciences model capabilities and building products to help scientists accelerate their research and leverage the full potential of AI for scientific work.

Rosalind Workbench brings together the scientific tools, data sources, interactive biology file viewers and core life sciences workflows into a central environment to help scientists investigate questions, design experiments, analyze results, and advance discovery. Rosalind Workbench can be used with any OpenAI model, including GPT-Rosalind--our dedicated life sciences model, which combines frontier reasoning with specialized tool orchestration across medicinal chemistry, genomics, wet-lab assistance, and other scientific applications. description:
About the Team:

About the Team: Our team brings OpenAI’s most capable technology to the world through our products. We've released ChatGPT, GPT6-Astra, and Codex. Across OpenAI’s enterprise product suite, it is critical to offer organizations the technology to securely establish, connect, and manage people and non-human identities across OpenAI products. The Enterprise Identity team builds shared identity foundations and enterprise controls for authentication and federation, provisioning and lifecycle, secure access, session management and revocation, administration, auditability, and access visibility so identity and access can be governed consistently across products. We build the foundational systems that enable organizations to adopt OpenAI products with confidence.. Our work underpins enterprise security, IT integration, and the safe deployment of AI at scale, making sure the right people have the right access at the right time.

We’re looking for an experienced Product Manager for OpenAI’s Enterprise Identity product efforts. You will lead efforts to deliver critical capabilities such as SSO, SCIM, and identity federation across all OpenAI products, enabling enterprises to securely manage users, data, and access in complex organizational environments.

This role requires close collaboration with engineering, security, GTM, and customer-facing teams to ensure our identity systems meet the needs of organizations ranging from high-growth startups to the world’s largest enterprises. Your work will directly enable safe, large-scale enterprise adoption of frontier AI.

  • Define the strategy and execute the roadmap for enterprise identity, spanning SSO, SCIM, and advanced admin controls.

title: Sr.Product Manager – Commerce Growth
description:
About HighLevel

About us
HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes.
To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value, demonstrating the impact of shared infrastructure at scale. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently.
Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability.

Our people
With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Our impact
Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that.
Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts

Role Overview

HighLevel processes payments at significant scale for the businesses that run on our platform and yet only a fraction of the businesses we serve have adopted payments at all. The constraint is structural rather than one of awareness: adoption is decided by the agencies who serve these businesses, and they have never had a commercial reason to act. We are hiring a Senior Product Manager - Commerce Growth to close that gap and make payments adoption the fastest-compounding line in our Commerce business.

This role owns the adoption and monetisation charter for Commerce end to end. It spans partner incentive design, the growth mechanics that move a business from signing up to transacting consistently, the partner-facing surfaces those programmes live in, and the commercial model underneath them. It is a general-management role as much as a product one, you will own the unit economics, the programme budget, and the evidence that the investment is working.

This role is ideal for product managers who have built growth or partner programmes at scale, who are comfortable being measured on a commercial outcome rather than a feature list, and who bring the analytical rigour to distinguish growth that was genuinely caused from growth that would have happened anyway.

What You'll Do

  • Own the payments adoption charter end to end - the strategy, roadmap and operating plan that take adoption and transacting volume to a multiple of today's levels, and the commercial targets attached to them.

  • Design, launch and iterate partner incentive programmes that make adoption commercially compelling for the agencies who drive it including eligibility models, qualification logic, payout mechanics and the controls that keep the programmes durable and abuse-resistant.

  • Own the partner-facing product surfaces where these programmes are discovered, understood and acted on progress, earnings and next-best-action, designed to scale to tens of thousands of partners without manual support.

  • Own the unit economics: customer acquisition cost, payback period, contribution margin and programme budget - modelled, forecast, and defensible to Finance and leadership.

  • Build a disciplined experimentation practice - randomised tests, holdout groups and incrementality measurement so that pricing and programme decisions are evidence-led rather than intuition-led.

  • Apply growth-hacking rigour across the adoption funnel: segmentation, lifecycle triggers, in-product prompts and targeted campaigns, in partnership with Lifecycle Marketing, Community and Support.

  • Lead commercial conversations with our largest agency partners, where bespoke arrangements rather than self-serve programmes are what move the number.

  • Own the monthly performance narrative - adoption, retention, cost efficiency and programme health and the decision to scale, hold or retire each initiative.

  • Partner with Analytics, Finance, Risk and Commerce platform engineering on the measurement, controls and infrastructure the charter depends on.

What Success Looks Like

  • Payments adoption grows at a multiple of its current rate, with the uplift demonstrably attributable to the work rather than to underlying trend

  • Incentive investment pays back inside its target window, measured on contribution rather than headline revenue

  • Partners understand what they have earned and why, without needing to contact support

  • Programme abuse remains negligible and is contained by automated controls rather than manual review

  • Programme spend tracks forecast, with variance understood and explained

Minimum Qualifications

  • 8–10 years of product management experience

  • Experience owning a growth, partner, referral or incentive programme where the commercial mechanic itself was the product

  • Comfort owning a commercial outcome end to end acquisition cost, payback, contribution margin and defending it to a finance audience

  • A track record of running controlled experiments and drawing the right conclusion from them, including the unwelcome one

  • Experience with payments, fintech, marketplaces or another business where unit economics are the product strategy

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in partner, reseller or franchise ecosystems where a third party not the end user makes the adoption decision

  • Familiarity with payment economics: processing rates, take rate, volume tiers, and how payment method mix affects platform monetisation

  • Experience designing abuse and fraud controls for a rewards, referral or affiliate programme

  • Background in vertical SaaS or platform businesses that monetise payments alongside subscriptions

Who This Role Is For

  • Product managers who think in unit economics, and who will hold the line when an initiative is popular but does not pay for itself.

  • PMs who treat commercial programmes as product surfaces with an interface, a rulebook and a feedback loop rather than a spreadsheet handed to marketing.

  • People energised by a very specific problem: getting tens of thousands of independent businesses to act on your behalf, repeatedly, at a price that makes sense.

Why Should You Join Us?

At HighLevel, we foster an exciting and dynamic work environment driven by a passionate team. We believe in a collective responsibility where no task is considered someone else's job. Our unwavering focus is on providing value to our users, and we achieve this by delivering solutions swiftly through lean principles, allowing us to bring products to market in a matter of weeks rather than quarters. Every good idea is put to the test, ensuring that we maintain a high standard of innovation. We prioritise the well-being of our team, recognizing that by taking care of them, they can better serve our users. We embrace the concept of continuous and iterative improvement, understanding that progress is an ongoing journey. We are also a well funded & profitable company.

Join us at HighLevel, and you will have the opportunity to learn the intricacies of scaling a B2B SaaS startup and develop impactful products that cater to the needs of our customers.

description:

About the Team

The Marketing OS – LeadGen Team owns the products and platform capabilities that help agencies attract, engage, capture, qualify, and understand leads across digital and offline customer journeys.

The team is responsible for:

  • Forms and form-building experiences

  • Surveys and customer data-collection workflows

  • Quizzes, assessments, and interactive lead-generation experiences

  • QR Codes and offline-to-online lead acquisition

  • Chat Widget and conversational lead capture

  • External Tracking across third-party websites and digital properties

  • Lead capture, submission, attribution, and behavioral analytics

  • Templates, integrations, embeddable experiences, and extensibility

These products are critical entry points into the HighLevel Marketing OS. They connect customer interactions across websites, landing pages, physical locations, campaigns, and external properties with HighLevel's CRM, automation, analytics, and communication capabilities.

Why Join HighLevel?

  • Ownership: It is never somebody else's job.

  • Customer focus: We are passionately focused on adding value for our users.

  • Speed: We use lean principles and go to market in weeks rather than quarters.

  • Experimentation: Good ideas are tested quickly, measured, and improved iteratively.

  • Growth: You will help scale a global B2B SaaS platform and build products used by millions of businesses.

  • People: We take care of our team so our team can take care of our users.

Role Overview

As Senior Product Manager – Marketing OS, LeadGen, you will help shape the future of lead generation at HighLevel.

You will own product strategy, roadmap, and execution across a portfolio that includes Forms, Surveys, Quizzes, QR Codes, Chat Widget, External Tracking, and adjacent lead capture and attribution capabilities.

Your mandate will be to evolve these products into a cohesive LeadGen experience that enables agencies and SMBs to create high-converting acquisition journeys, collect better-quality data, understand visitor behavior, and activate every lead through HighLevel's CRM and automation ecosystem.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You will work closely with Engineering, Design, and Data on your portfolio, partner with adjacent product teams on shared foundations, and help shape how HighLevel competes in lead generation, conversational engagement, behavioral tracking, and marketing attribution.

Your work will directly impact product adoption, lead volume, lead quality, engagement, conversion, retention, and overall platform growth.

Your Responsibilities

  • Own the LeadGen roadmap: Define and execute the product strategy and roadmap across Forms, Surveys, Quizzes, QR Codes, Chat Widget, and External Tracking.

  • Build cohesive experiences: Drive consistency across builders, templates, publishing, data models, integrations, analytics, and reporting.

  • Improve lead capture: Ship capabilities that increase visitor engagement, completion rates, lead quality, qualification, routing, and follow-up.

  • Connect the customer journey: Partner with CRM, Workflows, Conversations, Analytics, and Payments teams to connect interactions with downstream business outcomes.

  • Drive External Tracking: Define how HighLevel captures visitor behavior, conversions, identity, attribution, and campaign activity across third-party websites.

  • Strengthen analytics foundations: Contribute to consistent event taxonomies, instrumentation standards, and reporting across the LeadGen portfolio.

  • Drive AI-assisted creation: Deliver AI-powered creation, copy generation, logic recommendations, qualification, insights, and conversion optimization.

  • Improve cross-device experiences: Ensure creation and consumption experiences are intuitive, responsive, accessible, and performant across desktop, mobile, and tablet.

  • Partner on technical decisions: Work with Engineering on builders, embeddable widgets, APIs, submission pipelines, tracking scripts, identity resolution, and event infrastructure.

Experience

  • Experience owning a customer-facing product or product area end to end, from discovery through launch and iteration.

  • Experience defining and executing a roadmap across multiple related product areas.

  • Strong understanding of lead generation, customer acquisition, conversion optimization, qualification, and growth loops.

  • Experience with products such as forms, surveys, quizzes, chat widgets, analytics, attribution, tracking, or interactive content.

  • Familiarity with behavioral tracking, including page views, clicks, scrolls, field interactions, submissions, abandonment, and conversion events.

  • Understanding of event taxonomies, analytics instrumentation, data pipelines, experimentation, and marketing attribution.

  • Exposure to embeddable products such as widgets, scripts, SDKs, forms, or externally hosted experiences.

  • Familiarity with APIs, webhooks, CRM integrations, field mapping, workflow automation, and identity resolution.

  • Experience partnering with Engineering on frontend, backend, data, and infrastructure systems.

  • Strong product judgment, analytical ability, and UI/UX sensibility.

  • Ability to influence cross-functional partners and drive alignment without direct authority.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, decision-making, and stakeholder management skills.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with AI- or LLM-powered creation, conversational, or optimization products.

  • Experience building form builders, survey platforms, chat products, interactive content, or behavioral analytics tools.

  • Experience with first-party tracking, customer identity, attribution, consent management, or data governance.

  • Exposure to high-volume event ingestion, real-time analytics, experimentation, or personalization systems.

  • Experience building products for marketing agencies, SMBs, creators, or multi-location businesses.

title: Technical Program Manager, Multimodal
description:
About the Team

The Product & Platform teams at OpenAI are responsible for delivering the company’s most impactful offerings—such as ChatGPT, our API platform, and new enterprise capabilities—to a global and diverse customer base. These systems must perform at scale and deliver exceptional experiences to developers, consumers, and businesses alike.

The ChatGPT Multimodal team works across voice, image generation, and other multimodal experiences to turn frontier research capabilities into reliable products. The team connects product usage and failure patterns with research, evaluation, data, inference, capacity, and external partnerships so that model and product improvements translate into better experiences for users.

About the Role

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to build the flywheel that helps ChatGPT multimodal products learn from real-world usage and improve quickly. You will lead programs spanning production-signal mining, evaluation and data pipelines, research-to-production parity, multimodal capacity planning, and complex cross-functional dependencies for voice and image-generation launches.

You will work closely with product engineering, research, Human Data, inference and capacity teams, safety partners, and external vendors or product partners. Success requires technical depth, strong systems thinking, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to turn fragmented or manual work into durable mechanisms that teams adopt.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Build a system for mining production conversations and product signals to identify representative multimodal workflows, user needs, and failure modes.

  • Establish and maintain evaluations for the highest-priority multimodal behaviors and use cases, with clear coverage, quality standards, and ownership.

  • Package production signals into decision-ready data and evaluations that research teams can use to improve model behavior.

  • Measure whether model, prompt, configuration, and product changes produce meaningful improvements in multimodal evaluations and user outcomes.

  • Close gaps between research and production environments, including system prompts, sampling behavior, multimodal configurations, inference differences, and other sources of parity drift.

  • Create a repeatable process for reproducing product failures with research partners and validating fixes in the shipped experience.

  • Lead multimodal capacity planning by forecasting demand, translating it into GPU and serving needs, and managing headroom and reallocation tradeoffs for voice and image-generation workloads.

  • Improve the tooling and operating processes used to plan, launch, and operate multimodal capabilities as demand and model behavior evolve.

  • Coordinate targeted multilingual data collection across research, Human Data, and external vendors.

  • Drive cross-functional programs that multimodal launches depend on, including multimodal actor recruitment and selection and voice-related product partnerships across vehicles, smart speakers, and headphone ecosystems.

  • Create clear operating cadences, decision rights, metrics, risk management, and executive-ready communication across complex, time-sensitive programs.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have led technically complex programs across machine learning, multimodal products, model evaluation, data pipelines, inference, capacity, or large-scale product infrastructure.

  • Can move fluently between user-facing product behavior and the underlying model, evaluation, configuration, serving, and capacity systems.

  • Have built mechanisms that convert production signals into prioritized evaluations, data, engineering work, and measurable product improvements.

  • Can reason credibly about GPU demand, serving constraints, latency, reliability, quality, and launch tradeoffs.

  • Have closed research-to-production gaps and can drive structured debugging and validation across teams with different environments and incentives.

  • Turn manual or fragmented workflows into scalable tooling, clear ownership, and durable operating practices.

  • Lead effectively across research, engineering, product, operations, Human Data, and external partners without relying on direct authority.

  • Communicate crisply, make ambiguity tractable, and use metrics and evidence to drive decisions.

  • Thrive in ambiguous, scaling environments and can bring order to complex cross-functional work without losing pace.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

HighLevel’s Commerce platform is the system of record for how our customers sell — what they offer and how it is priced, how orders get fulfilled, and how money moves: payments in, invoices out, and books that balance. It spans product information, pricing, taxes, and channels; fulfillment and inventory; and the full finance stack of payments, checkout, invoicing, and ledger — together powering commerce for a global base of agencies and businesses operating at scale.

We are seeking a Group Product Manager, Commerce, to lead product across three connected verticals — Business Operations, Fulfillment Operations, and Finance — and the team of Product Managers who own them. You will set the strategy for the end-to-end commerce lifecycle, from catalog to cash, and be accountable for the coherence, reliability, and growth of the platform as a whole.

The ideal candidate is an experienced product leader who has managed and grown other Product Managers, and who can zoom from platform strategy down to the details of a pricing engine, a fulfillment flow, or a ledger entry. You lead through your team, raise the bar on product craft, and turn a broad, interdependent surface area into a clear, sequenced roadmap.

Your mission: To build a coherent, reliable, and extensible commerce platform — spanning what customers sell, how it is fulfilled, and how they get paid — and to build the team that delivers it, so HighLevel’s customers can run their entire business on us.

What You’ll Do

Set Commerce Product Strategy – Own the vision and multi-quarter roadmap across Business Operations, Fulfillment, and Finance, translating a broad, interdependent surface area into clear, sequenced priorities.

Lead & Grow a Team of PMs – Manage, mentor, and hire Product Managers across the verticals, setting a high bar for product craft and owning their performance, development, and career growth.

Own the End-to-End Commerce Lifecycle – Be accountable for the full catalog-to-cash journey — product information and pricing, fulfillment and inventory, payments, invoicing, and ledger — as one connected system.

Drive Platform Coherence – Ensure shared contracts like the analytics engine, layouts, and reporting are designed once and reused, so the verticals compose into a single, consistent platform rather than a set of silos.

Deliver Business Operations – Guide the PIM, pricing, taxes, channel configuration, loyalty, and analytics roadmap that lets merchants define what they sell, to whom, and at what price.

Deliver Fulfillment Operations – Steer fulfillment, inventory, and the upcoming warehousing, time-clocking, and metering charters so what was sold reliably reaches the buyer.

Deliver Finance – Own the payments, checkout, invoicing, and ledger/accounting roadmap, ensuring money moves securely and the books balance across providers and external systems like QuickBooks and Xero.

Own Outcomes & Metrics – Drive measurable growth in GMV, transaction success, merchant adoption, and reliability, using data to prioritize across a large and competing set of bets.

Partner with Senior Stakeholders – Work closely with engineering, design, finance, operations, and leadership to align on strategy, resourcing, and trade-offs, and represent Commerce in company-level planning.

Balance Delivery & Long-Term Bets – Keep near-term charters shipping on time while investing in the platform foundations that compound over the next several years.

Raise the Operating Bar – Establish the rituals, specs, and quality standards — discovery, prioritization, launch, and review — that make the team predictable, fast, and outcome-driven.

Experienced People Leader – You have managed and grown Product Managers, and you get energy from multiplying your impact through a strong, well-run team.

Platform & Commerce Depth – You have led product across commerce, payments, fintech, or a comparable transaction-heavy platform, and understand how catalog, fulfillment, and finance fit together.

Strategic and Execution-Focused – You can define a multi-vertical strategy and still hold your teams to crisp execution, ensuring ideas translate into shipped, measurable impact.

Systems Thinker – You see the interdependencies across modules and design for coherence, reuse, and shared contracts rather than one-off solutions.

Outcome- & Customer-Centric – You balance business goals, risk, and trust, keeping the merchants who run their business on the platform at the center of every decision.

Highly Data-Driven in Ambiguity – You are comfortable prioritizing across a broad, messy portfolio, using data to make sharp trade-offs without waiting for perfect information.



What You’ll Bring

  • 8+ years of Product Management experience, including 2+ years directly managing Product Managers, and 10+ years of total professional experience.

  • A track record of leading product across a large, multi-team surface area — ideally in commerce, payments, fintech, or platform/SaaS — with measurable business impact.

  • Proven people leadership: hiring, developing, and retaining strong PMs, and building the operating rhythm of a high-performing product team.

  • Strong platform and systems judgment, with the ability to reason about how pricing, fulfillment, payments, invoicing, and ledger interconnect.

  • Experience partnering with senior engineering, design, and business stakeholders to set strategy, secure resourcing, and drive company-level outcomes.

Bonus:

title: Product Manager II - Payment Orchestration
description:
About Us

HighLevel is an AI powered, all-in-one white-label sales & marketing platform that empowers agencies, entrepreneurs, and businesses to elevate their digital presence and drive growth. We are proud to support a global and growing community of over 2 million businesses, comprised of agencies, consultants, and businesses of all sizes and industries. HighLevel empowers users with all the tools needed to capture, nurture, and close new leads into repeat customers. As of mid 2025, HighLevel processes over 4 billion API hits and handles more than 2.5 billion message events every day. Our platform manages over 250 terabytes of data distributed across five databases, operates with a network of over 250 microservices, and supports over 1 million hostnames.

Our People

With over 1,500 team members across 15+ countries, we operate in a global, remote-first environment. We are building more than software; we are building a global community rooted in creativity, collaboration, and impact. We take pride in cultivating a culture where innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated, and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Our Impact

As of mid 2026, our platform powers over 1.5 billion messages, helps generate over 200 million leads, and facilitates over 20 million conversations for the more than 2 million businesses we serve each month. Behind those numbers are real people growing their companies, connecting with customers, and making their mark - and we get to help make that happen.

About the Role

The Payments Platform team at HighLevel builds and scales the payment orchestration layer that powers every transaction across our ecosystem from invoices and subscriptions to point-of-sale and mobile checkout. The orchestration platform is the engine that routes payments across providers, processes transactions, generates receipts, and ingests webhook events at scale, making it one of the most business-critical systems we run. This role is a rare opportunity to own core payments infrastructure that hundreds of thousands of businesses depend on every day.

We are seeking a Product Manager II, Payment Orchestration, who will own the roadmap and execution for HighLevel’s orchestration platform spanning the orchestrator, transaction lifecycle, receipts, and webhook ingress. You will be responsible for the reliability, breadth, and developer experience of the platform that every payment surface at HighLevel is built on top of.

The ideal candidate combines product judgment with technical fluency, comfortable reasoning about payment routing, PSP integrations, idempotency, and event delivery, while keeping adoption, transaction success, and customer trust at the center of every decision. This is a role for someone who wants to go deep on payments infrastructure and translate that depth into measurable product outcomes.

Your mission: To build a reliable, extensible, and provider-agnostic payment orchestration platform that maximizes transaction success and powers fast, secure, and seamless payment experiences across HighLevel’s global customer base.

What You’ll Do

Own the Orchestration Roadmap & Execution – Define and deliver the roadmap for the payment orchestration platform, spanning the orchestrator, transaction lifecycle, receipts, and webhook ingress, with a strong focus on reliability, coverage, and transaction success.

Drive Payment Routing & Provider Strategy – Improve authorization rates and cost efficiency through smart routing, provider selection, retries, and failover across multiple PSPs and gateways.

Own the Transaction Lifecycle – Lead the end-to-end handling of authorizations, captures, refunds, voids, and disputes, ensuring correctness, idempotency, and state integrity at scale.

Deliver Reliable Webhook Ingress – Build robust inbound webhook processing that normalizes, deduplicates, and reliably fans out provider events to downstream services with strong delivery guarantees.

Ship Trustworthy Receipts & Records – Own accurate, well-formatted receipts and transaction records that give customers and their end users clear, trustworthy proof of every payment.

Elevate Platform APIs & Developer Experience – Partner with engineering to design clean, well-documented payment APIs and events that internal teams and product surfaces can build on with confidence.

Champion Reliability & Observability – Treat uptime, latency, and error rates as first-class product metrics, driving instrumentation, alerting, and reconciliation to keep the platform accurate and dependable.

Ensure Scale, Security & Compliance – Own PCI, risk, and data-integrity considerations, ensuring the platform stays secure, scalable, and compliant as volume grows.

Collaborate Cross-Functionally – Work closely with engineering, design, data, risk, support, and partner-facing teams to align the platform with the needs of every payment surface it powers.

Leverage Payments Data for Decisions – Use metrics such as authorization rates, transaction success, failure reasons, latency, and reconciliation gaps to prioritize the roadmap and measure impact.

Own Outcomes, Not Just Features – Deliver measurable improvements in transaction success, platform reliability, and provider coverage, and in the experience of the teams building on the platform.


Who You Are

Payments & Platform Experience – You have built and shipped features within a payments, fintech, or platform/infrastructure ecosystem, delivering secure, reliable systems that operate at scale.

Technically Fluent – You can hold your own with engineers on APIs, webhooks, idempotency, routing logic, and failure modes, and you use that fluency to make sharper product decisions.

Reliability-Minded – You care deeply about correctness, uptime, and edge cases, and you design for the failure paths - retries, timeouts, duplicates, and reconciliation, not just the happy path.

Customer- & Developer-Centric – You balance business goals, risk, and trust, keeping the needs of both end customers and the internal teams who build on your platform at the center of your decisions.

Strategic and Execution-Focused – You can shape a clear roadmap for your area while staying deeply involved in execution to ensure ideas translate into shipped, measurable impact.

Highly Data-Driven in Ambiguity – You are comfortable working with messy, incomplete data - transaction logs, failure reasons, and provider quirks - to find patterns and derive actionable insights.


What You’ll Bring

  • 4+ years of Product Management experience, with a focus on payments, fintech, platform, or API/infrastructure products,

  • A track record of shipping impactful platform or infrastructure features that improved reliability, coverage, or transaction success in a high-scale environment.

  • A working understanding of payment systems PSP/gateway integrations, the authorization-to-settlement lifecycle, webhooks, idempotency, and reconciliation.

  • Strong technical fluency, with the ability to partner closely with engineering on API design, event models, and system trade-offs.

  • Familiarity with SaaS and platform growth levers, including adoption of internal platforms, developer experience, and reliability as a driver of customer trust.

Bonus:

  • You have worked on a payments or fintech platform processing significant transaction volume across multiple providers, and can clearly articulate your impact on reliability, authorization rates, and customer trust.


Why should you join us?

At HighLevel, we foster an exciting and dynamic work environment driven by a passionate team. We believe in a collective responsibility where no task is considered someone else's job. Our unwavering focus is on providing value to our users, and we achieve this by delivering solutions swiftly through lean principles, allowing us to bring products to market in a matter of weeks rather than quarters. Every good idea is put to the test, ensuring that we maintain a high standard of innovation. We prioritise the well-being of our team, recognizing that by taking care of them, they can better serve our users. We embrace the concept of continuous and iterative improvement, understanding that progress is an ongoing journey. We are also a well funded & profitable company.

Join us at High Level, and you will have the opportunity to learn the intricacies of scaling a B2B SaaS startup and develop impactful products that cater to the needs of our customers.

  • Drive project alignment by managing dependencies, guiding technical discussions, and making sure the right conversations happen at the right time
  • Anticipate risks and blockers, escalate when needed, and keep momentum toward resolution
  • Influence outcomes by building trusted, strong partnerships across the organization
  • Champion effective ways of working—finding the right balance of tools, structure & practices while continuously improving how we collaborate and deliver on our commitments

We'd love to hear from you if you have:

  • 5+ years of program and project management experience in a cloud/SaaS environment, supporting technology teams
  • Comfort diving into technical details to guide conversations and drive alignment, with the ability to adapt communication style — knowing when to dive deep and when to zoom out — for different audiences
  • The ability to thrive in ambiguity, operating with autonomy to create clarity and momentum
  • A track record of building a culture of knowledge-sharing and transparency through strong collaboration

  • PMP & Scrum Certifications
  • Prior experience with business systems that support QTC (billing platforms, Salesforce, NetSuite)
